source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Make Audio Foundation Models more Explainable
source.authors: Théo Mariotte; Martin Lebourdais; Antonio Almudévar; Marie Tahon; Alfonso Ortega; Nicolas Dugué

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figures are flattened in the text extraction, so their plotted values cannot be read precisely.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates sparse autoencoders on audio foundation models, but it does not test superposition, feature overlap geometry, polysemanticity, or SAE features in LLMs. Its results concern a related but different system type from the versions that specify LLMs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE probing, reconstruction, and factor-prediction results. These concern audio models and are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as evidence for versions that specify LLMs or toy networks. The paper does not report a superposition or feature-overlap measurement.
record.test_reason: The paper applies TopK SAEs to four audio foundation models (AST, WavLM, HuBERT, MERT) as an explainability tool. It reports only how well the SAE codes do: reconstruction MSE, probe accuracy, and DCI informativeness and completeness. It never mentions superposition, polysemantic neurons, feature geometry or LLMs. None of its results bear on V1–V6. V4 and V5 concern LLM representations, and the paper does not ask whether SAE features are canonical units of the model. The record's 'discusses'/T6 is inaccurate because the paper does not discuss superposition. It uses the SAE method, so T4 fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors say sparse codes do not improve informativeness, only completeness. They also report that reconstruction MSE worsens with sparsity, with WavLM best at 85%, and that completeness falls as factor entropy rises.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK SAEs trained on pretrained audio-model representations and evaluates classification and voice-factor prediction. It does not train toy networks with controlled feature sparsity or measure overlapping directions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with SAE sparsity; factor patterns also depend on model layer, especially for WavLM and HuBERT.

fits_no_version.finding: On four audio SSL models, TopK SAE codes (N=2048 from D=768) keep singing-technique probe accuracy and factor R² until very high sparsity. DCI completeness rises with sparsity above the original representations, and completeness falls as factor entropy rises.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TopK SAEs on audio foundation-model layers give sparse codes that retain task and voice-factor information while concentrating factor prediction into fewer dimensions.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: Several relevant outcomes are shown only in figures, with no numerical values stated in the text. The experiments use VocalSet and its 400-file test set, and the study does not evaluate feature overlap geometry or whether SAE dimensions are canonical model units.
record.rows_left_out: No separately plotted model-by-layer-by-sparsity points were transcribed from Figures 1 and 2; the paper's text reports the trends, while the plotted point values are not reliably recoverable from the flattened figure text.

untested.parts: No toy models, overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent phase transition or geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-competition analysis.
No study of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
Not LLMs. No measure of features spread across neurons; SAE recovery is not framed as evidence of superposition.
No test of SAE feature stability across seeds or sizes, of canonicality, or of completeness as model units.
No comparison of one-dimensional and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reconstruction MSE result (Fig. 1 right) and the factor-family-by-layer result (Fig. 4) have no rows, but neither bears on any version. The paper does not cite Toy Models of Superposition.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
No neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, or dedicated-versus-shared dimensions are tested.
No polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity are studied.
The study analyzes audio foundation models, not LLMs; it does not measure features spread across LLM neurons or assess LLM SAE dictionaries.
It measures completeness of predictions in SAE codes, but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features or superposition geometry is made.

rows.subject: AST, WavLM, HuBERT, and MERT
rows.size_stated: Each model has 13 transformer layers and a hidden vector of D = 768 dimensions; SAE code dimension N = 2048.
rows.operation_detail: Linear probes on TopK SAE representations predict singing-technique classes across sparsity levels.
rows.baseline: Original model representations; Table 1 reports selected-layer probe accuracies.
rows.value: Figure only; the text says sparsity has little effect overall compared with original representations.
rows.note: The paper reports the overall trend across the studied models and selected layers, not an aggregate numerical accuracy. It also says accuracy drops sharply at 99% sparsity.
rows.check: No version is linked, so a state against a version cannot be set. As a finding, probe accuracy stays near the original representations until it drops sharply at 99% sparsity (figure only). The record's 'partial' has no version referent.

rows.subject: AST
rows.size_stated: 13 transformer layers; hidden vector D = 768; SAE code dimension N = 2048.
rows.operation_detail: Linear probe on SAE representations across sparsity levels.
rows.baseline: Original model representations; selected-layer accuracies include 81.8% at layer 6 and 82.0% at layer 12.
rows.value: Figure only through 95% sparsity; the text states a sharp drop at 99%, with merely 20 active dimensions remaining.
rows.note: The narrative specifically describes AST as stable up to 95% sparsity and reports the 99% drop, but gives no SAE-probe accuracy values.
rows.check: No version is linked. The AST probe on SAE codes is stable to 95% sparsity and drops sharply at 99%, about 20 active dimensions. No SAE accuracy values are given in the text.

rows.subject: AST, WavLM, HuBERT, and MERT
rows.size_stated: Each model has 13 transformer layers and a hidden vector of D = 768 dimensions; SAE code dimension N = 2048.
rows.operation_detail: Lasso regressions from SAE codes predict eGeMAPS voice factors; informativeness is evaluated with R².
rows.baseline: Original non-sparse representations, shown as dashed reference lines.
rows.value: Figure only; the text says SAEs generally preserve informativeness, with degradation at very high sparsity.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation are plotted; numerical values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The paper reports a trend across models and layers, not a numerical aggregate.
rows.check: No version is linked. R² informativeness is preserved and degrades only at very high sparsity. The authors say informativeness is not improved over the original representations.

rows.subject: AST, WavLM, HuBERT, and MERT
rows.size_stated: Each model has 13 transformer layers and a hidden vector of D = 768 dimensions; SAE code dimension N = 2048.
rows.operation_detail: Lasso regressions from SAE codes predict eGeMAPS voice factors; completeness is evaluated.
rows.baseline: Original non-sparse representations, shown as dashed reference lines.
rows.value: Figure only; the text says completeness increases with sparsity and exceeds the original representations.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation are plotted; numerical values are not stated in the text.
rows.locator: Sections 4.2 and 4.3.1; Figure 2 (right); Takeaway after Section 4.3
rows.note: The authors interpret higher completeness as fewer dimensions being needed to predict a factor. This is an audio-model result and does not establish canonical SAE units.
rows.check: No version is linked. Completeness rises with sparsity and exceeds the original representations. This is a DCI disentanglement metric, not evidence that SAE features are canonical model units.
